research_mode: official Building Safety Regulator and GOV.UK primary guidance only; complaints, resident escalation, golden-thread information and key-building-information methodology gates; no parcel result or safety score claimed

sources.name: Golden-thread digital record
verified_claims: Clients, principal designers, principal contractors and accountable persons in scope must keep a digital building-information record.
limitations: The duty's applicability depends on role and building classification.

sources.name: Golden-thread purpose
verified_claims: The golden thread supports legal compliance and management of building safety.
limitations: Keeping records does not by itself demonstrate compliant or effective safety management.

sources.name: Regulator use of information
verified_claims: Fire and Rescue Services, BSR and building-control bodies may use golden-thread information.
limitations: Potential regulator use does not mean a regulator has reviewed a particular record.

sources.name: Digital and secure storage
verified_claims: Building information must be kept digitally and secure from unauthorised access.
limitations: A digital system is not necessarily secure without control evidence.

sources.name: Availability and usability
verified_claims: Information must be available when needed and presented in a usable way.
limitations: Technical availability does not prove that information is complete or understandable.

sources.name: Single source of truth
verified_claims: The record should operate as the building's single source of truth.
limitations: A designated system may still contain conflicting, stale or incomplete entries.

sources.name: Plain-English accessibility
verified_claims: Information should be accessible in a simple, understandable format and written in plain English.
limitations: Plain language does not remove the need for technical detail where safety decisions depend on it.

sources.name: Golden-thread GDPR compliance
verified_claims: Management and storage of the information must comply with GDPR.
limitations: A statement of compliance is not evidence of lawful processing in every instance.

sources.name: Client compliance records
verified_claims: The client must keep information describing the building and showing how building work complies with building regulations and duties.
limitations: A record of intended compliance is not proof that completed work complies.

sources.name: Project information sharing
verified_claims: The client must share building information with every designer and contractor on the project.
limitations: A sharing obligation does not prove receipt, understanding or use.

sources.name: Version-controlled system
verified_claims: The client's digital record-keeping system should use version control so changes can be seen.
limitations: Version history does not guarantee the correctness of each version.

sources.name: Building-control document set
verified_claims: The record-keeping system supports documents including plans, competence declarations, control plans, compliance statements and occurrence-reporting plans.
limitations: Document presence does not prove approval, competence or compliance.

sources.name: Completion information handover
verified_claims: At completion, building information must be handed to the relevant accountable or responsible person and receipt in a usable format confirmed.
limitations: A handover confirmation does not prove the recipient validated every document.

sources.name: Occupied-building core records
verified_claims: APs and PAPs must keep the health and safety file, safety case report, residents' engagement strategy and mandatory occurrence reporting system information.
limitations: Record retention does not establish that the underlying duties are performed effectively.

sources.name: Information sharing on request
verified_claims: Building information must be provided on request to BSR, other accountable persons and residents or residential-unit owners.
limitations: Disclosure may still be limited by data protection and lawful restrictions.
